title: Governing Kind of Proof When Recent Evidence Exists (PAP Supply Replenishment Program)
content:
**Decision rule.** On a resupply schedule of the PAP Supply Replenishment Program that accepts either compliance data or a practitioner note as proof of continued use, the kind of proof that governs is decided by how recent the evidence is:

- when the download that proves continued use has a window that ended within the last 90 days, that download governs, at its credited date, and a practitioner note is not used;
- when no such download ended within the last 90 days but a re-evaluation documenting benefit is dated within the last 90 days, that note's visit date governs.

When neither holds, this recency rule selects nothing. On a schedule that accepts only one kind of proof, the rule does not apply.

## Decision table

| Download proving continued use: window ended within 90 days | Re-evaluation documenting benefit dated within 90 days | Governs |
|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | the download's credited date (the note is not used) |
| yes | no | the download's credited date |
| no | yes | the note's visit date |
| no | no | not decided by this rule |

"Within the last 90 days" counts calendar days from the window's last night, or from the note's visit date, to the handling day: 90 days or fewer is within; 91 or more is not.

## Cases (hypothetical)

- The download proving continued use has a window that ended 40 days ago and is credited at that night; a re-evaluation documenting benefit is dated 10 days ago. The download governs, even though the note is newer.
- The download proving continued use has a window that ended 120 days ago; a re-evaluation documenting benefit is dated 60 days ago. The note's visit date governs.
- Window ended exactly 90 days ago: within the last 90 days, so the download governs.

The download and the re-evaluation are those on the patient's device record under PAP Therapy Equipment.
